引言：企业知识管理的新分水岭

在当今数字化与智能化交织的商业环境中，企业每天都在产生海量的数据、文档与流程记录。传统的企业知识库（如网盘、Wiki、文档管理系统）长期充当着“知识网盘”的角色。然而，随着信息量的爆炸式增长，传统知识库的弊端日益凸显：“查找两小时，阅读五分钟”、文档版本混乱、知识孤岛林立，导致大量高价值的企业沉淀沦为“死知识”。

2026年，大语言模型（LLM）与AI Agent（智能体）技术的爆发式成熟，为企业知识管理带来了范式革命。数商云凭借深厚的技术积淀与行业前瞻性，推出了数商云2026企业级AI知识库。这一创新系统打破了传统静态文档的束缚，将知识库从一个“被动检索的静态仓库”升级为“主动思考、协同执行的动态智能体（Agent）”，全面定义了新一代企业级知识系统。

items.content:
Last week, OpenAI's revenue chief Denise Dresser suddenly left her role after just eight months at the company. She was tasked with growing OpenAI's enterprise unit, a high-margin part of the business that aims to directly take on the company's chief rival, Anthropic.

Dresser's departure came just two days after another longtime executive, Brad Lightcap, said he was ending an eight-year stint at the ChatGPT creator to "start something new." Dresser took over many of Lightcap's responsibilities in April, when OpenAI said he was transitioning his position as operating chief to a new role focused on "special projects."

OpenAI namedDali Rajic, former COO of cybersecurity company Wiz, which Google acquired for $32 billion earlier this year, as its new chief revenue officer.

items.title: The Hottest AI Models Aren't the Ones Developers Actually Use - Business Insider
items.summary: All-MiniLM-L6-v2, a fast, light-weight model released in 2021 by Sentence Transformers, was download
items.content:
All-MiniLM-L6-v2, a fast, light-weight model released in 2021 by Sentence Transformers, was downloaded 1.55 billion times in the first 7 months of 2026 despite receiving just 5,156 likes. Also, not a single model released in 2026 made Hugging Face's top 25 by downloads, while 13 of the 25 were released in 2022.

Smaller models, those under 1 billion parameters —the numerical values a model learns during training that help determine how it processes and generates outputs — account for 83% of all-time downloads among Hugging Face repositories that disclose their parameter counts. Larger models, those with more than 100 billion parameters — such as Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 — account for just 1% [...] Moonshot's Kimi K3, for instance, arrived with 2.8 trillion parameters and generated a ton of buzz in Silicon Valley for its coding performance and lower price. But it was only downloaded about 60 times per like it received, which is low, Hugging Face said.

Alibaba's Qwen model series has taken a different approach, spanning a wider range of sizes. Hugging Face says that breadth has helped make Qwen part of developers' "default workflow" for fine-tuning and deployment — and it has translated into much higher usage. Qwen models logged about 2 billion downloads in 2026, roughly 55 times Moonshot's 37 million. [...] That gap between hype and usage is also showing up in how companies deploy AI. Pinterest, for example, previously told Business Insider that it takes a "model-agnostic" approach, using its own models for personalization, open-source AI models when they offer better economics, and closed models when they perform best.

items.summary: A deterministic function was used to convert pixel measurements to millimeters. For this purpose, th
items.content: A deterministic function was used to convert pixel measurements to millimeters. For this purpose, the mesiodistal width of the right maxillary and the right mandibular central incisors was measured for each patient using digital intraoral scanners and recorded in Microsoft Excel. For patients missing the right central incisor, the left central incisor was used as an alternative reference. After data collection, the mean mesiodistal width was calculated from the learning set only (maxillary: 8.44 mm; mandibular: 5.28 mm) and used as a reference value for pixel to millimeter conversion in the proposed AI framework. For each image, the mesiodistal width of the central incisor was manually annotated as a pixel distance by four independent dental examiners. This annotated pixel distance was [...] must make an initial treatment decision solely based on a visual examination of the dental arch, without access to additional clinical information. Additionally, this study aimed to statistically evaluate the proposed AI framework against dental specialists. Although several studies have explored CNN and ML methods using intraoral photographs for the automated detection, segmentation, and treatment planning across various dental conditions, to our knowledge, an AI framework that directly identifies S-TES from occlusal images while also supporting preliminary triage has not been reported. [...] This study investigated the feasibility of developing and evaluating an AI framework to provide preliminary triage support using only occlusal images in S-TES cases without considering implant-based interventions. As shown in Fig. 1, a CNN object detection model (YOLOv8m) was used to detect the S-TES and its adjacent teeth. items.summary:
August 17, 2026 by The Neuron

Researchers at the Institute of Fundamental and Frontier Sciences, Un
items.content:
August 17, 2026 by The Neuron

Researchers at the Institute of Fundamental and Frontier Sciences, University of Electronic Sciences and Technology of China have combined boson sampling, a quantum process with experimentally verified advantage over classical computers, with neural networks to improve machine learning classification. The team developed a hybrid framework where a neural network compresses data features onto a boson sampling circuit, generating quantum states that enhance support vector machine performance. Using four datasets with various classes, the model outperformed classical linear and sigmoid kernels, demonstrating the potential of boson sampling-based quantum kernels for practical quantum-enhanced machine learning. [...] ## Hybrid Boson Sampling-Neural Network Architecture for Enhanced Classification

The core innovation lies in a neural network’s ability to compress complex data features, preparing them for processing by a programmable boson sampling circuit. This approach addresses a significant hurdle in quantum machine learning: the high dimensionality of practical datasets. The team’s framework utilizes the neural network to reduce the number of features needed for analysis, bridging the gap between large, complex data and the limitations of current quantum hardware. items.content: Artists are often recognizable through collections of distinctive patterns (‘fingerprints’) in their work. Identifying such traits has important applications in authorship attribution, education, cultural heritage research and historical analysis. Here we focus on music, a domain with a rich tradition of theoretical and mathematical analysis. We train a variety of supervised learning models to identify 20 iconic jazz musicians from a curated dataset of 84 h of recordings. In particular, we introduce a multi-input architecture that represents four musical domains separately: melody, harmony, rhythm and dynamics. This design allows us to accurately identify individual performers (our best model obtains 94% accuracy across 20 classes) and to examine which musical elements most strongly [...] Machine learning provides a more scalable method for learning artistic fingerprints. The standard approach is to train a supervised learning model to identify the creator of an artwork from a given input. items.title: AI hiring tools can invent their own bias, research finds - HR Executive
items.summary: When the researchers ran a version of the test where groups genuinely did perform differently, forci
items.content:
When the researchers ran a version of the test where groups genuinely did perform differently, forcing a diversity objective into the mix lowered overall success rates. The intervention only helps when the underlying population truly is equivalent, and confirming that requires a judgment call.

The paper, presented at the International Conference on Machine Learning in 2026, tested a synthetic hiring scenario with invented demographic labels, not a live enterprise system. Its authors are careful to note the mechanism, not the specific numbers, as the transferable finding. Still, as more HR tools move from single-decision scoring toward agentic systems that learn and adapt across a series of choices, the question the study raises deserves a place in procurement conversations. [...] Despite those equal odds, the models developed unequal patterns, repeatedly putting different fictional groups into different categories of jobs. The authors link the result to an early, random success or failure can lead a decision-maker to repeat apparently successful job pairings rather than test alternatives. The same dynamic has been documented in the human experiments that inspired the task

That finding discounts what most HR technology buyers have been told to expect. Standard fairness benchmarks, the kind vendors cite when they say a model has been tested for bias, generally show newer models performing better over time. This research measured whether a model builds a new stereotype from its own decision history.

The AI industry tends to obsess over the newest frontier models: the biggest releases, the strongest benchmark scores, and the launches that dominate social media. Developers, meanwhile, often stick with smaller and older models that are cheap, stable, and already embedded in production systems.

items.title: Sick of A.I. Slop? So Are Tech Giants. - nytimes.com
items.summary: The digital sewage heap has sprawled across tech platforms, cheapening meaningful content and pollut
items.content:
The digital sewage heap has sprawled across tech platforms, cheapening meaningful content and polluting the information ecosystem, as chatbots and video generators continue to advance.

Now, Silicon Valley wants to take out the trash.

Spotify, a music streamer, said it removed 75 million bulk uploads, duplicate songs and other “spammy” tracks last year — a sizable chunk of its total portfolio. LinkedIn said in July that “A.I. slop is a top priority for all of us” and developed a button for users to report it. Researchers from YouTube’s parent company, Google, described how a video service wiped 130,000 channels of low-quality content off its platform over six months. items.title: AI Pushes Educators to Focus On the Art of Teaching, Lesson Design - govtech.com
items.summary: Booker says AI is a "wake-up call," as teachers begin to modify what they're doing to achieve specif
items.content:
Booker says AI is a "wake-up call," as teachers begin to modify what they're doing to achieve specific learning outcomes for students. Some curriculum will have to change, he said, but another key aspect of success in education will be digital citizenship — teachers and students learning to live and work responsibly in a world transformed by AI.  
  
Taking away the focus from the final product is not necessarily a negative, Booker said. The process is where the real learning happens, he said, when teachers are giving feedback along the way and students improve based on that feedback. [...] "Why do I need this? I'm a good teacher without AI," Garpstas recalled saying to herself. "I had all the reasons not to use it, but I didn't have a choice. I had to take the class."  
  
She said the class confirmed some of her fears about AI — that it could spread misinformation, replace critical thinking and exploit private data — and introduced new fears about kids becoming attached to AI chatbots or companions. But overall, she said learning the capabilities AI offers "transformed" her.  
  
"This is going to make a huge difference for me as a teacher creating things and finding activities," Garpstas said. It's a "huge timesaver."  
  
Garpstas, though cautious about the technology, is excited by what AI can do, but other teachers are more hesitant and not as optimistic. [...] "Without good governance and culture, it would be like the wild west that was once cellphones, where without intentional usage it will be just a wasteland," Solanco High School teacher Josh Fleming said.  
  
But with good governance, teachers say AI can level the playing field for students with differing needs by putting an assignment in a student's native language or simplifying the language for a student with special needs, or adding rigor to assignments for gifted students.
